plainTranslation: Friction and pull in the same breath. You want each other and rub each other wrong - fights that turn into heat, heat that turns into fights. Failure mode: the fighting becomes the fuel and you confuse intensity for intimacy. Aim the charge at desire, not combat, and notice if the spark needs conflict to stay lit, because that burns out.
policy: Governed by synastry-policy. Descriptive, not deterministic; intensity is never treated as obligation, safety concerns override astrology.

summaryShort: This is attraction with some edge to it. Venus and Mars want each other, but they don't move together easily. The chemistry is real, but it can come with irritation, mixed signals, and that feeling that the other person knows exactly how to get under your skin.
summaryDeep:
This is attraction with some edge to it. Venus and Mars want each other, but they don't move together easily. The chemistry is real, but it can come with irritation, mixed signals, and that feeling that the other person knows exactly how to get under your skin.

There may be a lot of heat here, but not all heat is intimacy. Sometimes the charge comes from being challenged. Sometimes it comes from feeling provoked. The trick is knowing the difference between passion and a pattern that keeps making you tense.

Failure mode: confusing friction for chemistry and staying because the conflict makes the connection feel alive.

Use the charge for something you're building together. Don't keep turning it on each other.
